summary_zh: 在克里斯塔·派克（Christa Pike）处决加利福尼亚州州长加文·纽瑟姆（Gavin Newsom）失败后，民主党的举动阻止了未来州长对这些人的处决
body_en: Gavin Newsom commutes more than 500 death sentences in California | Gavin Newsom
Democrat’s move prevents these people from executions under future governors, after Christa Pike’s failed execution

Gavin Newsom , California ’s governor, commuted the death sentences of more than 500 people on the state’s death row on Thursday, a move that ensures they can never be executed under future administrations.

The Democrat ’s mass commutation at the end of his term has converted all of the state’s death sentences to life without the possibility of parole, the largest clearing of any US death row in modern history.
The move comes after the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee sparked global outrage and renewed calls for a nationwide pause on capital punishment .
His decision affects 529 men and 19 women who were sentenced to death in the state, making up the largest death row in the western hemisphere, the governor said in a letter announcing his decision.

“I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us,” he wrote. “I know we cannot execute people in our imperfect legal system and remain true to our core values, first among them justice and human decency.”

Newsom, considered a probable candidate for president in 2028, has long opposed the death penalty and issued a moratorium on executions in 2019. He also dismantled the state’s physical death row chamber in the infamous San Quentin prison, transferring people with death sentences to other facilities where they had more freedom of movement and access to programs – for some, a dramatic change after decades isolated in solitary cells .
Calls grow for US death penalty halt after ‘torturous’ botched execution of Christa Pike

The last execution in California was in 2006, but hundreds of people incarcerated in the state’s prisons have continued to live under death sentences, making California home to the largest death row population in the nation.

Newsom’s office noted on Thursday that of the 548 people sentenced to death, 220 of them had waited 15 years or more to be appointed habeas counsel, the legal representation they are entitled to access to fight their cases. And 139 people have waited 20 years or more for representation. If there were no moratorium in place, 45 people in the state are considered to have exhausted their appeals and would be immediately subject to execution.

“This decision is among the most difficult of my career, not because I doubt its necessity for our state but because I know its announcement may surface excruciating memories for victims’ families,” Newsom said. “I hold this painful truth along with the belief that this is a righteous action.”
The California supreme court will have to review and approve the clemency grants for cases where the individual was convicted of multiple felonies, Newsom said.

The announcement was praised by the American Civil Liberties Union and prominent advocates who oppose the death penalty, including Martin Luther King III, the eldest son of the civil rights icon, and Bryan Stevenson, an internationally renowned death penalty lawyer.

Jeanne Woodford, a former California prisons director who oversaw four executions, applauded Newsom in a statement, noting that more than 200 people nationwide had been exonerated after being sentenced to death: “As someone who has carried out executions in California, I am haunted by the fear that we will execute an innocent person.”

A relative of a victim killed by one man on California’s death row also spoke out in favor of the commutations. Jess Nichol is the sister of Polly Klaas, a 12-year-old killed in 1993 in a notorious case that paved the way for tough-on-crime laws. She said in a statement on Thursday that she used to support the execution of the man who killed her sister. “But over time I’ve realized that whether he’s executed has absolutely nothing to do with my recovery or with real public safety. The system tells survivors that execution matters to our healing. It doesn’t. It’s a distraction from what we actually need,” she said.

Governors of both parties have taken bold measures to oppose capital punishment over the years, including an Illinois Republican who commuted all 167 death sentences in 2003 before leaving office. In 2024, North Carolina’s Democratic governor, Roy Cooper, commuted 15 death sentences in the state in his final day in office.

Support for the death penalty has been declining across the US, but Democrats at times have been reluctant to do mass commutations out of fear that Republicans will paint them as “soft on crime” politicians who sided with people convicted of brutal murders.

Newsom has supported criminal justice reform efforts, including changes to prioritize rehabilitative programs in prisons . But some advocates over the years have accused him of caving to political pressures on the issue, including when he has vetoed the release of high-profile prisoners even after they have been granted parole .
body_zh: 加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom) 在加州减刑了 500 多名死刑犯加文·纽瑟姆
在克里斯塔·派克（Christa Pike）处决失败后，民主党的举动阻止了这些人在未来州长的领导下被处决
加州州长加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom) 周四对该州 500 多名死囚减刑，此举确保他们在未来的政府领导下永远不会被处决。
这位民主党人在任期结束时进行的大规模减刑，将该州所有死刑判决都改为无期徒刑，且不得假释，这是美国现代历史上对死囚牢房最大规模的清理。
此前，田纳西州克里斯塔·派克处决失败引发了全球的愤怒，并再次呼吁在全国范围内暂停死刑。
州长在宣布其决定的信中表示，他的决定影响了该州被判处死刑的 529 名男性和 19 名女性，这是西半球最大的死囚牢房。
他写道：“我采取这一行动是因为我坚信，国家批准的杀戮与加州的价值观不相容，破坏了我们法律体系的基础，并削弱了我们每个人的能力。” “我知道我们无法在不完善的法律体系中处决人，并忠于我们的核心价值观，首先是正义和人类尊严。”
纽瑟姆被认为是 2028 年总统的可能候选人，长期以来一直反对死刑，并于 2019 年宣布暂停执行死刑。他还拆除了臭名昭著的圣昆廷监狱的州实体死囚室，将死刑犯转移到其他设施，在那里他们有更多的行动自由和参与项目的机会 — — 对一些人来说，这是在单独牢房隔离数十年后的巨大变化。
克里斯塔·派克“惨遭”拙劣处决后，要求美国停止死刑的呼声越来越高
加州最后一次执行死刑是在 2006 年，但该州监狱中仍有数百名被判处死刑的人继续生活，这使得加州成为全美死囚人数最多的州。
纽瑟姆办公室周四指出，在 548 名被判处死刑的人中，其中 220 人等待了 15 年或更长时间才被任命为人身保护律师，这是他们有权获得的法律代表来打官司。 139 人等待代表权已达 20 年或更长时间。如果没有暂停执行，该州有 45 人将被视为已用尽上诉权，将立即被处决。
纽瑟姆说：“这个决定是我职业生涯中最困难的决定之一，不是因为我怀疑它对我们州的必要性，而是因为我知道它的宣布可能会给受害者家属带来痛苦的记忆。” “我坚持这个痛苦的事实，并相信这是一个正义的行动。”
纽瑟姆说，加州最高法院将必须审查并批准对个人被判犯有多项重罪的案件的宽大处理。
这一声明受到了美国公民自由联盟和反对死刑的知名人士的赞扬，其中包括民权偶像马丁·路德·金三世的长子和国际知名死刑律师布莱恩·史蒂文森。
负责监督四起处决的加州前监狱长珍妮·伍德福德 (Jeanne Woodford) 在一份声明中对纽瑟姆表示赞赏，并指出全国有 200 多人在被判处死刑后被无罪释放：“作为在加州执行过死刑的人，我担心我们会处决一个无辜的人。”

加州死囚牢房中被一名男子杀害的受害者的一名亲属也公开表示支持减刑。杰西·尼科尔 (Jess Nichol) 是波莉·克拉斯 (Polly Klaas) 的妹妹，波莉·克拉斯 (Polly Klaas) 12 岁，于 1993 年在一起臭名昭著的案件中被杀，这为严厉打击犯罪的法律铺平了道路。她在周四的一份声明中表示，她曾经支持处决杀害她妹妹的男子。 “但随着时间的推移，我意识到他是否被处决与我的康复或真正的公共安全完全无关。系统告诉幸存者，处决对我们的康复很重要。事实并非如此。这分散了我们真正需要的注意力，”她说。
多年来，两党州长都采取了大胆措施反对死刑，其中包括一位伊利诺伊州共和党人，他在 2003 年离任前对所有 167 名死刑犯进行了减刑。 2024 年，北卡罗来纳州民主党州长罗伊·库珀 (Roy Cooper) 在其任期的最后一天对该州 15 名死刑犯进行了减刑。
美国各地对死刑的支持率一直在下降，但民主党人有时不愿进行大规模减刑，因为担心共和党人会把他们描绘成“对犯罪软弱”的政客，站在被判犯有残酷谋杀罪的人一边。
纽瑟姆支持刑事司法改革努力，包括优先考虑监狱康复计划的改革。但多年来，一些支持者指责他在这个问题上屈服于政治压力，包括他否决释放知名囚犯，即使他们已获得假释。

title_en: US holds secret talks with Tehran to deport Iranians even as war drags on, court documents show
title_zh: 法庭文件显示，即使战争仍在继续，美国仍与德黑兰举行秘密会谈，以驱逐伊朗人
summary: Trump administration push emerges from a lawsuit alleging violations of national immigration regulations The Trump administration held secret talks with Iran on deporting Iranians even as the war there dragged on, court documents obtained by the Associated Pre
summary_zh: 特朗普政府的推动源于一项指控违反国家移民法规的诉讼 特朗普政府与特朗普政府举行了秘密会谈
body_en: Trump administration push emerges from a lawsuit alleging violations of national immigration regulations
The Trump administration held secret talks with Iran on deporting Iranians even as the war there dragged on, court documents obtained by the Associated Press show.

The court documents unsealed on Thursday show the Republican administration as recently as mid-October said it had plans to deport the Iranians through an unnamed third country, although it was unclear when it intended to do so.

The judge in the case ordered the government to give the court 24-hour notice of any finalized plans to deport Iranians to Iran or to any other country and five days’ written notice before any such deportation is carried out.

“We are at war with a country where the president of the United States has said, as recently as two or three days ago, if not yesterday, that it is essentially lawless … A country that is an enemy of the United States, according to the current president. A country that, according to our president, murdered tens of thousands of protestors,” the judge, Ana Reyes, said according to the 15 October transcript that has now been unsealed.

“And what you’re telling me is that the United States of America is going to send individuals back to that region, facing what you and I and everyone who would ever look at this would know would be, at a minimum, a serious threat of certain death.”
“Yes, your honor,” justice department attorney Dimitar Georgiev-Remmel said. “The government is executing lawful orders of removal.”

Georgiev-Remmel told the court there was no specific date set to carry out any removals. A legal group representing Iranians held by Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) said a dozen Iranian detainees had been given notice over the past week that they would be deported to Iran. The legal group, the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund, brought the lawsuit in which the transcript was released.

The court documents show that the administration maintained contacts with Iranian officials during the war over the removals, specifically for submitting travel documents and figuring out “possible avenues for removal”.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), ICE’s parent agency , and the state department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The development emerged from an ongoing lawsuit that alleges the Trump administration’s immigration agencies have been sharing confidential information about Iranian asylum seekers with the Iranian government, violating national immigration regulations and endangering countless Iranians, court filings argue.

The Iranian American Legal Defense Fund said on Thursday at least 12 Iranian detainees have been contacted by the Iranian Interest Section, an Iranian representative office in the Pakistani embassy in Washington that handles consular affairs, in the past week and notified of an upcoming deportation flight to Iran through Pakistan. The group did not say when the deportation would occur.

One of those detainees attempted suicide once he learned he might be returned to Iran, according to Yasmine Chubin, the executive director of the organization. He was one of two people who were subsequently moved across state lines to a detention center in Texas, where detainees are often relocated immediately preceding a removal.
None of the detainees who have been contacted have been provided any information in writing from immigration authorities, the legal group said.
Activists abroad have expressed concern about deportees returning to Iran, whose theocracy has been cracking down on intellectuals and where the government vociferously cracks down on any dissent.

The lawsuit depicts a coordinated campaign between the US and Iranian governments to identify Iranians in ICE custody and pressure them to return to Iran – a marked departure from decades of diplomatic hostility between the two governments. The DHS has denied that it is sharing asylum application records with the Iranian government.

Hundreds of emails exchanged between US immigration officials exposed how the two countries worked together to arrange for more than 100 Iranians to be flown back to Iran on three immigration flights in September and December 2025 and January 2026.

During the 15 October hearing, Reyes warned government attorneys that she would initiate contempt proceedings if the administration violated her order to give the court advance notice of any planned deportation flights.
“We are talking about sending individuals in our care and custody to a country that we have bombed and we may continue bombing, and is a declared enemy of this country,” Reyes said.
body_zh: 特朗普政府的推动源于一项指控违反国家移民法规的诉讼
美联社获得的法庭文件显示，特朗普政府与伊朗就驱逐伊朗人问题进行了秘密会谈，尽管那里的战争仍在拖延。
周四公布的法庭文件显示，共和党政府最近在 10 月中旬表示，计划通过未透露姓名的第三国驱逐伊朗人，但尚不清楚其打算何时这样做。
该案法官命令政府就任何将伊朗人驱逐到伊朗或任何其他国家的最终计划提前 24 小时通知法院，并在执行任何此类驱逐之前提前五天书面通知。
根据现已启封的 10 月 15 日笔录，法官安娜·雷耶斯 (Ana Reyes) 表示：“我们正在与一个国家交战，美国总统就在两三天前甚至昨天还曾表示，这个国家本质上是无法无天的……根据现任总统的说法，这个国家是美国的敌人。根据我们的总统的说法，这个国家谋杀了数万名抗议者。”
“你告诉我的是，美利坚合众国将把一些人送回那个地区，面对你和我以及所有关注此事的人都知道，至少会面临死亡的严重威胁。”
“是的，法官大人，”司法部律师迪米塔·格奥尔基耶夫-雷梅尔说。 “政府正在执行合法的驱逐令。”
格奥尔基耶夫-雷梅尔告诉法庭，目前还没有确定具体的搬迁日期。一个代表被移民和海关执法局（ICE）关押的伊朗人的法律团体表示，过去一周已有十几名伊朗被拘留者接到通知，称他们将被驱逐到伊朗。法律团体伊朗裔美国人法律辩护基金会提起了诉讼，并公布了诉讼记录。
法庭文件显示，政府在战争期间就驱逐事宜与伊朗官员保持着联系，特别是提交旅行证件和找出“可能的驱逐途径”。
ICE 的上级机构国土安全部 (DHS) 和国务院没有立即回应置评请求。
法庭文件称，这一进展源于一项正在进行的诉讼，该诉讼指控特朗普政府的移民机构一直与伊朗政府分享有关伊朗寻求庇护者的机密信息，违反了国家移民法规，并危及无数伊朗人。
伊朗美国法律辩护基金会周四表示，过去一周，巴基斯坦驻华盛顿大使馆负责处理领事事务的伊朗代表处伊朗利益科联系了至少 12 名伊朗被拘留者，并通知他们即将通过巴基斯坦飞往伊朗。该组织没有透露何时会进行驱逐。
该组织执行主任亚斯敏·楚宾 (Yasmine Chubin) 表示，其中一名被拘留者在得知自己可能被遣返伊朗后试图自杀。他是随后被跨州转移到德克萨斯州拘留中心的两人之一，被拘留者经常在被转移之前立即被重新安置。
该法律组织表示，所联系的被拘留者均未收到移民当局的任何书面信息。
国外的活动人士对被驱逐者返回伊朗表示担忧，伊朗的神权政治一直在打压知识分子，政府也大力镇压任何异议。
该诉讼描绘了美国和伊朗政府之间协调一致的行动，以识别被 ICE 拘留的伊朗人，并迫使他们返回伊朗 — — 这明显背离了两国政府之间数十年的外交敌对状态。国土安全部否认与伊朗政府分享庇护申请记录。
美国移民官员之间交换的数百封电子邮件揭露了两国如何合作，安排100多名伊朗人在2025年9月、2025年12月和2026年1月乘坐三趟移民航班返回伊朗。
在 10 月 15 日的听证会上，雷耶斯警告政府律师，如果政府违反她向法院提前通知任何计划的驱逐航班的命令，她将启动藐视法庭诉讼。
雷耶斯说：“我们正在讨论将我们照顾和拘留的人员送往我们轰炸过的国家，我们可能会继续轰炸，并且他们是这个国家的敌人。”

The Trump administration has escalated its economic campaign against Cuba

The Trump administration on Thursday escalated its economic campaign against Cuba , issuing a determination that clears the path for U.S. sanctions on several crucial sectors of the island's economy while also targeting Chinese-based suppliers to Havana's military forces.

The sanctions are part of a larger effort by President Donald Trump and his allies to force political change in Havana even as the country continues to grapple with a deepening economic and energy crisis that has suffocated its population.
With the new penalties the State Department is expanding its reach to target new sectors of Cuba's economy, including electronics, manufacturing, marine and technology.

“Cuba’s ruling elite is hoarding the island’s energy, shipping, and technology resources for its own enrichment, leaving the Cuban people to contend with blackouts, shortages, and a stagnant economy,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement.

In total, eight entities and two individuals were targeted, including China National Electronic Import and Export Company and Beijing H & C Technologies, two China-based companies that the U.S. is accusing of procuring weapons and selling surveillance and security equipment to the Cuban government.
Captain identified after deadly Florida Learjet crash

Learjet with 9 aboard crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida: FAA
Washington's campaign against Havana has only accelerated in recent months, with public spats between their representatives at the United Nations and on social media.

Last week, the U.N. General Assembly condemned the U.S. economic embargo of Cuba for the 34th year. But the U.S. campaign to influence the outcome led a number of countries to vote against the resolution or sit out the decision for the first time.

Meanwhile, Trump's threat in late January to impose tariffs on any country that sells or provides oil to Cuba has made islandwide blackouts even more common, while daily outages in Cuba now surpass 24 hours as the aging grid fails and fuel reserves dwindle.

特朗普政府周四升级了针对古巴的经济行动，发布了一项决定，为美国对该岛经济的几个关键部门实施制裁扫清了道路，同时也针对哈瓦那军队的中国供应商。
这些制裁是唐纳德·特朗普总统及其盟友为迫使哈瓦那进行政治变革而做出的更大努力的一部分，尽管该国仍在努力应对日益严重的经济和能源危机，该危机已导致其民众窒息。
通过新的处罚措施，国务院正在扩大制裁范围，瞄准古巴经济的新领域，包括电子、制造、海洋和技术。
美国国务卿马可·卢比奥在一份声明中表示：“古巴的统治精英正在囤积岛上的能源、航运和技术资源，以谋取私利，使古巴人民面临停电、短缺和经济停滞的困境。”
总共有八个实体和两名个人成为攻击目标，其中包括中国电子进出口公司和北京宏创科技有限公司，美国指控这两家中国公司向古巴政府采购武器并向古巴政府出售监控和安全设备。

华盛顿针对哈瓦那的攻势近几个月来才有所加速，两国驻联合国代表和社交媒体上的公开争吵不断。
上周，联合国大会谴责美国对古巴实施的第34年经济封锁。但美国影响结果的行动导致一些国家首次投票反对该决议或袖手旁观。
与此同时，特朗普在一月下旬威胁要对任何向古巴出售或供应石油的国家征收关税，这使得全岛停电变得更加普遍，而随着老化的电网故障和燃料储备的减少，古巴每天的停电时间现在超过24小时。

body_en: The judge oversaw extradition proceedings in Mexico for a Canadian citizen allegedly helping Ryan Wedding
A Mexican judge has been arrested and accused of accepting $2m in bribes in exchange for releasing a suspected Canadian drug trafficker from custody, US officials said on Thursday.

Luis Benítez Alcántara was overseeing extradition proceedings in Mexico in 2024 for Canadian citizen Andrew Clark, who was charged in the US with helping to run a billion-dollar drug-trafficking group allegedly headed by the former Canadian Olympic snowboarder Ryan Wedding, the justice department said in a statement.
Ryan Wedding’s journey from Olympic snowboarder to alleged cocaine kingpin
Benítez is accused of releasing Clark from custody after accepting the bribe payments, according to the statement.
Clark was arrested days after his release and removed to the United States, where he faces drug-trafficking and murder charges.
The statement said Benítez, 49, was arrested on Sunday in Colombia. He is charged in a nine count indictment with being an accessory after the fact. It was not immediately known if he has a lawyer.
US officials will request Benítez’s extradition from Colombia, the statement said.

“Crooked public officials, no matter where they are, who assist drug traffickers operating here at home will face justice in the United States,” the US attorney general, Todd Blanche, said in the statement.

It is the latest arrest in the US investigation into a multinational drug-trafficking network allegedly run by Wedding, who became a top FBI fugitive accused of moving cocaine from Latin America into the United States and orchestrating several killings. Wedding was arrested in Mexico earlier this year and flown to California, where he pleaded not guilty to murder and drug charges.

Dozens of people have been arrested in connection with the alleged drug network, and authorities seized large volumes of drugs, weapons and cash, as well as millions of dollars’ worth of automobiles, motorcycles, artwork and jewelry in its investigation.
Clark’s attorney, Matthew Lombard, did not immediately respond to messages on Thursday.
body_zh: 法官在墨西哥监督了一名涉嫌帮助瑞安婚礼的加拿大公民的引渡程序
美国官员周四表示，一名墨西哥法官已被捕，并被指控收受 200 万美元贿赂，以换取释放一名加拿大毒贩嫌疑人。
司法部在一份声明中称，路易斯·贝尼特斯·阿尔坎塔拉正在墨西哥监督 2024 年加拿大公民安德鲁·克拉克 (Andrew Clark) 的引渡程序，后者在美国被指控帮助运营一个价值数十亿美元的贩毒集团，据称该集团由前加拿大单板滑雪运动员瑞安·威丁 (Ryan Wedding) 领导。
瑞安·威丁 (Ryan Wedding) 从奥林匹克滑雪运动员到涉嫌可卡因头目的历程

克拉克在获释几天后被捕，并被送往美国，在那里他面临贩毒和谋杀指控。

这是美国对据称由威丁经营的跨国贩毒网络进行的调查中最新逮捕的一起，威丁成为联邦调查局的一名头号逃犯，被指控将可卡因从拉丁美洲运送到美国并策划了多起杀戮。维丁今年早些时候在墨西哥被捕，并飞往加利福尼亚州，在那里他对谋杀和毒品指控不认罪。
数十人因涉嫌毒品网络而被捕，当局在调查中查获了大量毒品、武器和现金，以及价值数百万美元的汽车、摩托车、艺术品和珠宝。

body_en: Harmeet Dhillon, controversial head of DoJ’s civil rights division, steps down | US midterm elections 2026
Dhillon is first high-level justice department official to leave after historic Republican defeat in 2026 midterms
Harmeet Dhillon, a Donald Trump ally who led the justice department’s civil rights division, is leaving her position.

“Today, I accepted the resignation of Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon, who led the Civil Rights Division with conviction the past 18 months. She has defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favor. The Department is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavors,” the attorney general, Todd Blanche, said in a post on X .

Dhillon is the first high-ranking justice department official to leave after the midterm elections in which Democrats took control of Congress. Democrats are expected to use that power to aggressively investigate executive agencies, including the justice department. Dhillon’s departure was first reported by Bloomberg Law.

Dhillon dramatically transformed the civil rights division in a little over a year and a half there, reorienting its mission away from the work it had traditionally done protecting the civil rights of minorities. Under her leadership, the department dropped many cases alleging discrimination against racial minorities in voting, housing, employment and education. Scores of career lawyers also left the division under her leadership, leading to an exodus of expertise of civil rights enforcement.
Harmeet Dhillon: DoJ lawyer a top contender for Trump’s retribution mission

Dhillon aggressively pursued claims of discrimination at universities, including claims that minorities were unfairly favored in admissions and claims of antisemitism against Jewish students. A whistleblower has said that investigations into the schools were conducted with a predetermined outcome and that lawyers were told to find a reason to file a lawsuit.

The civil rights division also oversaw investigations into the killing of US citizens Alex Pretti and Renee Nicole Good by federal agents in Minnesota during an immigration enforcement surge – neither has resulted in criminal charges.

“From day one, Harmeet Dhillon abdicated her responsibility to enforce our nation’s federal civil rights laws and destroyed the crown jewel of the justice department,” said Kristen Clarke, who led the civil rights division under Joe Biden and is now general counsel at the NAACP.
“Instead of protecting the civil rights of all Americans, she abandoned cases, purged the work force and weaponized the division to target institutions to achieve illegitimate, partisan goals.”

The division also had some high-profile failures under Dhillon’s watch. It sued more than two dozen states for voter roll information and lost every single case. Several of the judges who ruled against the department were appointed by Donald Trump

“Harmeet Dhillon has been the most destructive, lawless and hateful head of the civil rights division in DoJ history,” said Stacey Young, a former civil rights division lawyer who now leads the group Justice Connection, a group for justice department alumni.

She added: “After she upended the division’s mission-critical work, the civil servants who dedicated their careers to protecting vulnerable communities were instead told to target them – and more than three-quarters of the division’s lawyers left. Dhillon wielded the enormous power of the justice department to threaten universities, state and local officials, and election workers in spurious cases that rarely won in court.”

A prolific poster on X, Dhillon would sometimes reveal civil rights investigations on the platform, a move that startled longtime justice department lawyers because the department has a longstanding practice of not speaking publicly about investigations. She has also publicly used a slur for people with disabilities, whose civil rights her division is charged with protecting. She has also described conservative influencers as “hoes” .

Dhillon grew up in Smithfield, North Carolina, after being born in India and then living in the UK and New York. “There were Klan signs on the highway where I grew up. I’m used to being an outsider. My superpower is not really caring what people think about me,” she told the Dartmouth alumni magazine last year.
Before joining the government, Dhillon ran her own law firm and was vice-chair of the California GOP. After the 2020 election, she worked on lawsuits contesting the election results.
body_zh: 备受争议的司法部民权部门负责人哈米特·迪隆 (Harmeet Dhillon) 辞职 | 2026 年美国中期选举
迪隆是共和党在 2026 年中期选举中历史性失败后第一位离职的司法部高级官员
唐纳德·特朗普的盟友、司法部民权部门负责人哈米特·迪隆 (Harmeet Dhillon) 即将离职。
“今天，我接受了助理总检察长哈米特·迪伦 (Harmeet Dhillon) 的辞职，她在过去 18 个月里以有罪的态度领导了民权部门。她捍卫了每个美国人的公民自由，并毫无畏惧或偏袒地执行法律。司法部感谢她热心的公共服务，我们祝愿她在未来的工作中一切顺利，”总检察长托德·布兰奇 (Todd Blanche) 在 X 上的帖子中说道。
迪隆是民主党控制国会的中期选举后第一位离职的司法部高级官员。预计民主党人将利用这一权力积极调查包括司法部在内的行政机构。彭博法律首先报道了迪隆离职的消息。
迪隆在一年半多的时间里对民权部门进行了戏剧性的转变，将其使命从传统上保护少数群体民权的工作中转移出来。在她的领导下，该部门撤销了许多指控少数族裔在投票、住房、就业和教育方面受到歧视的案件。数十名职业律师也离开了她领导下的部门，导致民权执法方面的专业知识外流。
哈米特·迪伦（Harmeet Dhillon）：司法部律师是特朗普报复任务的最佳竞争者
迪隆积极追究大学歧视的指控，包括少数族裔在招生中受到不公平对待的指控以及针对犹太学生的反犹太主义指控。一名举报人表示，对学校的调查是有预定结果的，律师被告知要找到提起诉讼的理由。
民权部门还监督了对明尼苏达州联邦特工在移民执法激增期间杀害美国公民亚历克斯·普雷蒂（Alex Pretti）和蕾妮·妮可·古德（Renee Nicole Good）的调查，但两人均未受到刑事指控。
“从第一天起，哈米特·迪隆就放弃了执行我们国家联邦民权法的责任，并摧毁了司法部皇冠上的明珠，”乔·拜登领导下的民权部门负责人、现任全国有色人种协进会总法律顾问克里斯汀·克拉克说。
“她没有保护所有美国人的公民权利，而是放弃了案件，清洗了劳动力，并将该部门武器化，以针对机构来实现非法的党派目标。”
在迪隆的领导下，该部门也遭遇了一些引人注目的失败。它起诉了二十多个州，要求提供选民名册信息，但每一起案件都败诉。几名做出对该部门不利裁决的法官是由唐纳德·特朗普任命的
“哈米特·迪隆是司法部历史上最具破坏性、无法无天和最可恨的民权部门负责人，”前民权部门律师史黛西·杨(Stacey Young)说，她现在领导着司法部校友组织“正义连接”(Justice Connection)。
她补充道：“在她颠覆了该部门的关键任务工作后，那些致力于保护弱势社区的公务员反而被告知要以他们为目标——该部门超过四分之三的律师离开了。迪隆利用司法部的巨大权力，在虚假案件中威胁大学、州和地方官员以及选举工作人员，而这些案件很少在法庭上获胜。”
Dhillon 是 X 上多产的发帖者，有时会在平台上揭露民权调查，这一举动令司法部的长期律师感到震惊，因为该部门长期以来一直不公开谈论调查。她还公开诽谤残疾人，而她的部门负责保护残疾人的公民权利。她还将保守派影响者描述为“锄头”。
迪伦出生于印度，后来居住在英国和纽约，之后在北卡罗来纳州的史密斯菲尔德长大。 “我长大的高速公路上有三K党的标志。我已经习惯了成为局外人。我的超能力并不真正关心人们对我的看法，”她去年告诉达特茅斯校友杂志。
在加入政府之前，迪伦经营着自己的律师事务所，并担任加州共和党副主席。 2020 年大选后，她参与了针对选举结果的诉讼。

title_en: Paraguay's president is impeached minutes after resigning following a bank collapse
title_zh: 巴拉圭总统因银行倒闭辞职几分钟后被弹劾
summary: Paraguayan lawmakers voted to impeach President Santiago Peña minutes after his resignation, as the collapse of a digital bank tied to his government froze millions of people's savings.
summary_zh: 巴拉圭立法者在总统圣地亚哥·佩纳辞职后几分钟投票弹劾他，因为与他的政府有关的数字银行倒闭了
body_en: A demonstrator holds a mock U.S. dollar bill depicting Paraguayan President Santiago Peña during a protest against the government and Ueno Bank, which Paraguay's central bank seized amid a solvency crisis, in Asunción, Paraguay, Wednesday. Jorge Saenz/AP hide caption

ASUNCIÓN, Paraguay — Paraguayan President Santiago Peña announced his resignation Thursday after the collapse of a major digital bank tied to his government triggered widespread protests, froze millions of people's savings and cost him the support of his own party.

The crisis at Ueno Bank turned Peña's long-ruling Colorado Party against him, a stunning reversal for the former International Monetary Fund economist who had enjoyed the backing of the country's most powerful politicians and was welcomed in Washington just weeks ago as a key ally of the Trump administration.

Minutes after Peña's announcement, the lower house voted 78-0 to impeach him, sending the charges to the Senate. Congressional leaders were expected to accept his resignation later Thursday, clearing the way for Vice President Pedro Alliana to be sworn in without waiting for a Senate trial.

Opposition senators were still demanding a trial, arguing that allowing Peña to resign would preserve his eligibility to become a senator for life, with legal protections that could prevent his prosecution.
Paraguay President Santiago Peña speaks to the media at United Nations headquarters, Sept. 19, 2023. Ted Shaffrey/AP hide caption

As lawmakers debated his impeachment, Peña said in a video posted to X that he was stepping down in the interest of "the stability of our country, social peace and the need to preserve our democratic institutions."

Even Peña's mentor, Colorado Party leader and former President Horacio Cartes, backed impeachment, saying the party would not side with "the plundering of public and private funds and pensioners' money." The United States Treasury sanctioned Cartes in 2023 over bribery allegations that the Trump administration lifted last year.

Peña, who until last year held a stake in a company linked to Ueno, expressed contrition. But he stopped short of accepting responsibility for the turmoil, which has left millions of depositors, retirees and workers scrambling to recoup their frozen savings and unpaid wages.
"I want to apologize to the people if I have failed them at any point," he said. "It was never my intention to betray the trust they placed in me."
The turmoil has hit Paraguay's currency. The guaraní fell nearly 4% against the U.S. dollar Thursday, bringing its losses this week to nearly 7%, according to central bank exchange-rate data.

Ueno Bank, which exploded from an obscure finance company to a household name in less than five years, claimed more than 60% of Paraguay's adults as customers. Many Paraguayans are left asking how a bank linked to the president could grow so rapidly in size and importance despite repeated warnings about its lending practices.

The answer lies in the uncomfortable proximity of Peña's Colorado Party to the country's regulators and business elite, a weakness that has endured even as steady economic management and rapid growth recently earned Paraguay coveted investment-grade credit ratings.
"Santiago Peña and the Colorado Party have stolen all our savings," said Luis Pineda, one of the protesters marching to Congress on Wednesday. "We are fed up with 70 years of plunder."

Soon after winning its banking license in 2023, Ueno seemed to be everywhere in Paraguay. The digital lender, a rebranded version of a decades-old finance company, lured customers with generous cash-back offers on groceries, grew to more than 70 locations, sponsored Paraguay's national soccer team and plastered its name on the country's main stadium.

Government money poured into Ueno's coffers under Peña. He also appointed Carlos Carvallo, president of Financiera Ueno, the predecessor to Ueno Bank, to run the central bank, the agency charged with supervising the digital lender.

As of last month, Ueno reported holding roughly $800 million in public deposits, about a quarter of its total, including money from the state pension and health fund and the operators of Paraguay's giant hydroelectric dams.

Even as retirees' savings and other public money piled up at Ueno, worries were escalating inside the central bank. In June, its inspectors found a pattern of risky lending to insiders, reported ABC Color, a leading Paraguayan newspaper. Ueno had extended large sums to companies tied to its owners, beyond what the law allows and without enough collateral to cover the debts if they went bad.
As recently as last month, Peña defended Ueno and the central bank's oversight, dismissing the concerns as a smear campaign that was spooking the public.
body_zh: 周三，在巴拉圭亚松森，一名示威者在抗议政府和上野银行时举着一张描绘巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩纳的模拟美元钞票。上野银行是巴拉圭央行在偿付能力危机中没收的。豪尔赫·萨恩斯/美联社隐藏标题栏
巴拉圭亚松森——周四，巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩纳宣布辞职，原因是一家与巴拉圭政府相关的大型数字银行倒闭，引发了广泛的抗议活动，冻结了数百万人的储蓄，并使他失去了自己政党的支持。
上野银行的危机使佩纳长期执政的科罗拉多党对他不利，这对这位前国际货币基金组织经济学家来说是一个惊人的逆转，他曾得到该国最有权势的政客的支持，几周前作为特朗普政府的重要盟友在华盛顿受到欢迎。
佩纳宣布这一消息后几分钟，下议院以 78 比 0 的投票结果弹劾他，并将指控送交参议院。预计国会领导人将于周四晚些时候接受他的辞职，为副总统佩德罗·阿利亚纳无需等待参议院审判就宣誓就职扫清道路。
反对派参议员仍然要求进行审判，认为允许佩纳辞职将保留他终身成为参议员的资格，并提供法律保护以防止他被起诉。
巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩纳于 2023 年 9 月 19 日在联合国总部向媒体发表讲话。Ted Shaffrey/美联社 隐藏标题栏
当议员们就弹劾案进行辩论时，佩纳在发布到 X 的视频中表示，他是为了“我们国家的稳定、社会和平以及维护我们民主制度的需要”而辞职。
就连佩纳的导师、科罗拉多党领袖、前总统奥拉西奥·卡特斯也支持弹劾，称该党不会支持“掠夺公共和私人资金以及养老金领取者的资金”。美国财政部于 2023 年对卡特斯实施了制裁，原因是特朗普政府去年撤销了卡特斯的贿赂指控。
佩尼亚直到去年还持有一家与上野有关联的公司的股份，他表达了悔意。但他没有承认对这场动乱负责，这场动乱导致数百万储户、退休人员和工人争先恐后地收回被冻结的储蓄和拖欠的工资。
他说：“如果我在任何时候让人们失望了，我想向他们道歉。” “我从来没有打算背叛他们对我的信任。”
这场动荡已经打击了巴拉圭的货币。根据央行汇率数据，周四瓜拉尼兑美元汇率下跌近 4%，本周跌幅接近 7%。
上野银行在不到五年的时间里从一家名不见经传的金融公司发展成为家喻户晓的名字，拥有超过 60% 的巴拉圭成年人客户。许多巴拉圭人不禁要问，尽管一再对其放贷行为发出警告，但与总统有联系的银行为何规模和重要性能够如此迅速增长。
答案在于佩尼亚领导的科罗拉多党与该国监管机构和商界精英的关系令人不安，尽管稳定的经济管理和快速增长最近为巴拉圭赢得了令人垂涎的投资级信用评级，但这一弱点仍然存在。
“圣地亚哥·佩纳和科罗拉多党偷走了我们所有的积蓄，”周三游行到国会的抗议者之一路易斯·皮内达说。 “我们厌倦了70年的掠夺。”
2023 年获得银行牌照后不久，上野似乎就遍布巴拉圭的各个角落。这家数字贷款机构是一家拥有数十年历史的金融公司的更名版，通过慷慨的食品杂货现金返还优惠吸引客户，业务扩展到 70 多个地点，赞助巴拉圭国家足球队，并将自己的名字印在该国的主体育场上。
政府资金涌入佩纳领导下的上野的金库。他还任命上野银行前身 Financiera Ueno 行长卡洛斯·卡瓦洛 (Carlos Carvallo) 负责运营中央银行，该机构负责监管这家数字贷款机构。
截至上个月，上野报告称持有约 8 亿美元的公共存款，约占其总存款的四分之一，其中包括来自国家养老金和医疗基金以及巴拉圭巨型水力发电大坝运营商的资金。
尽管退休人员的储蓄和其他公共资金堆积在上野，央行内部的担忧仍在升级。据巴拉圭主要报纸 ABC Color 报道，今年 6 月，该公司的检查人员发现了向内部人士提供高风险贷款的模式。上野向与其所有者相关的公司提供了大量资金，超出了法律允许的范围，而且如果这些公司出现坏账，也没有足够的抵押品来偿还债务。
就在上个月，佩尼亚为上野和央行的监督进行了辩护，称这些担忧是一场吓唬公众的抹黑运动。

title_en: Head of Justice Department office on Civil Rights resigns
title_zh: 司法部民权办公室主任辞职
summary: The head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, Harmeet Dhillon, is out after 18 tumultuous months in charge.
summary_zh: 司法部民权司司长 Harmeet Dhillon 在经历了 18 个月的动荡任期后下台。
body_en: Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon, accompanied by her aides, speaks during a news conference at the Justice Department in Washington, D.C., on Sept. 29, 2025. Dhillon resigned on Thursday. Andrew Harnik/Getty Images hide caption

The head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, Harmeet Dhillon, is out after 18 tumultuous months in charge, during which she radically reshaped the unit's mission, oversaw the mass exodus of career staff, and aggressively pursued President Trump's agenda.
Dhillon is the first senior department official to depart the Trump administration since Democrats retook control of the House and Senate in midterm elections.
Attorney General Todd Blanche, in a statement on X, announced Dhillon's resignation and thanked her for her service.

"She has defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favor," he wrote. "The Department is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavors."
In her own statement, Dhillon said the job had been "the honor of a lifetime."
"We ushered in the downfall of illegal DEI, we fought to protect women in girls' sports, and so much more," she added.
Reshaped civil rights mission at Justice Department transforms its work, workforce

During her tenure, Dhillon implemented dramatic changes in the Civil Rights Division, pushing out roughly 300 career attorneys, hiring inexperienced ideological allies to replace them, and using the division's enforcement powers to advance Trump's MAGA policies.

The changes marked a dramatic shift for the division, which was created some 70 years ago during the civil rights movement to end racial segregation in the U.S. For decades, it fought to protect the constitutional rights of all Americans across all aspects of life, from housing and employment to education and policing.

Dhillon, a conservative attorney and Trump loyalist, came into office with a different view. In her eyes, the division had narrowed its mission in recent decades to only protecting the rights of people of color, and she promptly shifted to aggressively pursuing conservative priorities.
"We don't just slow down the woke," she said at a Federalist Society event in 2025. "We take up the cause to achieve the executive branch's goals."
Trump's push to reshape the DOJ's civil rights division sparks mass exodus of attorneys

Under her leadership, the division redirected its energies to enforce Trump's executive orders, including ending the alleged radical indoctrination in schools, defending women from "gender ideology extremism," and combatting antisemitism and purported anti-Christian bias.
In the run-up to the midterm elections, the Civil Rights Division sued dozens of states demanding they turn over voter information — in furtherance of Trump's allegations of voter fraud.
Election officials pushed back, and courts tossed the department's lawsuits.

The division also accused numerous universities and law schools of discriminating against white and Asian students, and sued UCLA and Harvard for allegedly allowing antisemitism to flourish on campus.
Judge dismisses Trump administration's antisemitism lawsuit against Harvard
In an email to division staff, Dhillon said she informed Trump in early October that she planned to return to private practice after the midterms, and now is the time to do so.
body_zh: 2025 年 9 月 29 日，负责民权事务的助理司法部长哈米特·迪隆 (Harmeet Dhillon) 在助手的陪同下，在华盛顿特区司法部举行的新闻发布会上发表讲话。迪隆于周四辞职。安德鲁·哈尼克/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
司法部民权司司长哈米特·迪伦 (Harmeet Dhillon) 在经历了 18 个月的混乱任期后离职，在此期间，她彻底重塑了该部门的使命，监督了职业员工的大规模外流，并积极推行特朗普总统的议程。
迪隆是自民主党在中期选举中重新控制众议院和参议院以来第一位离开特朗普政府的高级部门官员。
司法部长托德·布兰奇在 X 的一份声明中宣布迪隆辞职，并感谢她的服务。
他写道：“她捍卫了每个美国人的公民自由，并毫无恐惧或偏袒地执行法律。” “该部门感谢她热心的公共服务，我们祝愿她在未来的工作中一切顺利。”
迪隆在自己的声明中表示，这份工作是“一生的荣幸”。
“我们迎来了非法 DEI 的垮台，我们为保护女子体育运动中的女性而奋斗，等等，”她补充道。
司法部重塑民权使命改变其工作和员工队伍
在她的任期内，迪隆对民权部门实施了巨大的变革，解雇了大约 300 名职业律师，聘请了缺乏经验的意识形态盟友来取代他们，并利用该部门的执行权来推进特朗普的 MAGA 政策。
这些变化标志着该部门的巨大转变。该部门是在大约 70 年前结束美国种族隔离的民权运动期间创建的。几十年来，该部门一直致力于保护所有美国人在生活各个方面的宪法权利，从住房和就业到教育和治安。
迪隆是一名保守派律师，也是特朗普的忠实拥护者，他上任时持有不同的观点。在她看来，近几十年来，该部门已将其使命缩小到仅保护有色人种的权利，而她迅速转向积极追求保守派的优先事项。
她在 2025 年联邦党人协会的一次活动上表示：“我们不只是让人们慢下来。我们致力于实现行政部门的目标。”
特朗普推动重塑司法部民权部门引发律师大规模外流
在她的领导下，该部门将精力转向执行特朗普的行政命令，包括结束学校中所谓的激进灌输，保护妇女免受“性别意识形态极端主义”的侵害，以及打击反犹太主义和所谓的反基督教偏见。
在中期选举前夕，民权部门起诉数十个州，要求他们交出选民信息，以进一步证实特朗普关于选民欺诈的指控。
选举官员予以反击，法院也驳回了该部门的诉讼。
该部门还指控许多大学和法学院歧视白人和亚裔学生，并起诉加州大学洛杉矶分校和哈佛大学，指控其允许反犹太主义在校园内盛行。
法官驳回特朗普政府针对哈佛大学的反犹太主义诉讼
迪隆在给部门工作人员的一封电子邮件中表示，她于 10 月初通知特朗普，她计划在中期选举后重返私人诊所，现在是时候这样做了。

title_en: Russell Brand is convicted of rape, and judge says he'll get a prison term
title_zh: 拉塞尔·布兰德被判强奸罪，法官称他将被判入狱
summary: A prosecutor described Brand as a ruthless, calculating, manipulative "sexual predator." Brand, 51, denied the charges, saying he had never forced anyone to do something against their will.
summary_zh: 一名检察官将布兰德描述为一个无情、精于算计、善于操纵的“性掠夺者”。 51 岁的布兰德否认了这些指控，称他从未强迫过任何人
body_en: Russell Brand is convicted of rape. The judge says he'll get a prison term : NPR

Russell Brand is convicted of rape. The judge says he'll get a prison term A prosecutor described Brand as a ruthless, calculating, manipulative "sexual predator." Brand, 51, denied the charges, saying he had never forced anyone to do something against their will.
Comedian and actor Russell Brand reflected in a car window as he left Southwark Crown Court in London on Monday. Alberto Pezzali/AP hide caption
London — Russell Brand was convicted Thursday of rape and sexual assault charges involving four women on allegations dating back more than 20 years.

Judge Joel Bennathan said the British actor-comedian faces a "significant" prison term when he is sentenced Monday. Brand had been free, but the judge rejected a bail request because of the possibility he might flee and he was taken into custody.
"I regret the hardship caused to the children, of course," the judge said. "But the hardship has been caused by serious criminal offending by their father."
Brand was a ruthless, calculating, manipulative "sexual predator," prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones said at trial.
Brand, 51, denied the charges and testified that he was obsessed with sex as a young man and once led a promiscuous life but had never forced anyone to do something against their will.
He was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Brand closed his eyes as the guilty verdict on the rape count was read but showed no emotion otherwise. When bail was denied, he gestured to his lawyers that he was OK and repeatedly said, "I'm good, I'm good, I'm good," before being taken away.

Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy of London's Metropolitan Police said the conviction was "a testament to the extraordinary courage, resilience and determination of the women who came forward and reported what happened to them."
"Brand used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually offend against women," he said. "As his profile grew, so too did his sense of entitlement."
The jury of eight men and four women in Southwark Crown Court deliberated more than eight hours over two days.

Known for risqué stand-up routines and battles with drugs and alcohol, Brand rose to prominence in the early 2000s, hosting television programs and his own BBC radio show. He appeared in Hollywood films including Forgetting Sarah Marshall and Get Him to the Greek and was briefly married to pop star Katy Perry.

In recent years he has moved away from mainstream media, relocated to Florida and built a large online following with videos mixing wellness, conspiracy theories and discussions of his religious devotion.
Brand was convicted of sexually assaulting a woman during a birthday party at a London bar in 2004, but cleared of orally raping her in a restroom.
He was also found guilty of kissing and groping another woman at a London radio station in 2004 or 2005 and of anally raping a fan he met backstage at one of his comedy shows in 2009.
The final conviction was for sexually assaulting a different woman who says the comedian demanded a massage and pressed his face into her groin during the recording of an advertisement in 2009.

Brand was acquitted of raping another woman in a hotel room during the Labour Party's annual conference in the seaside town of Bournemouth in 1999, and of attempting to indecently assault a woman by dragging her into the men's bathroom at the London office of music channel MTV.
body_zh: 拉塞尔·布兰德被判犯有强奸罪。法官称他将被判入狱：NPR
拉塞尔·布兰德被判犯有强奸罪。法官称他将被判入狱一名检察官将布兰德描述为一个冷酷无情、精于算计、善于操纵的“性掠夺者”。 51 岁的布兰德否认了这些指控，称他从未强迫任何人做违背自己意愿的事情。
周一，喜剧演员兼演员拉塞尔·布兰德离开伦敦南华克刑事法庭时，映在车窗里。阿尔贝托·佩扎利/美联社隐藏标题栏
伦敦——周四，拉塞尔·布兰德 (Russell Brand) 被判犯有强奸和性侵犯罪，涉及四名女性，这些指控可以追溯到 20 多年前。
乔尔·本纳森法官表示，这位英国喜剧演员周一被判刑时将面临“重大”监禁。布兰德已获释，但法官因他可能逃跑而拒绝了保释请求，因此被拘留。
“当然，我对给孩子们造成的困难感到遗憾，”法官说。 “但困难是由他们父亲的严重刑事犯罪造成的。”
检察官里尔·卡米-琼斯在审判中表示，布兰德是一个冷酷无情、精于算计、善于操纵的“性掠夺者”。
51 岁的布兰德否认了这些指控，并作证说，他年轻时沉迷于性，曾经过着放荡的生活，但从未强迫任何人做违背他们意愿的事情。
他被判犯有一项强奸罪和三项性侵犯罪。他的两项强奸罪名和一项企图猥亵罪名被判无罪。
当强奸罪的有罪判决被宣读时，布兰德闭上了眼睛，但没有表现出任何其他情绪。当保释被拒绝时，他向律师示意自己没事，并反复说：“我很好，我很好，我很好”，然后被带走。
伦敦大都会警察局侦探警司安迪·弗菲表示，这一定罪“证明了那些站出来报告自己遭遇的女性所具有的非凡勇气、韧性和决心。”
“布兰德利用他的影响力、地位和名气来剥削和性侵犯女性，”他说。 “随着他的知名度不断提高，他的权利意识也随之增强。”
南华克皇家法院的陪审团由八名男性和四名女性组成，在两天内审议了八个多小时。
布兰德以有伤风化的单口喜剧表演以及与毒品和酒精的斗争而闻名，他在 2000 年代初期声名鹊起，主持电视节目和自己的 BBC 广播节目。他出现在好莱坞电影中，包括《忘记莎拉·马歇尔》和《带他去希腊》，并与流行歌星凯蒂·佩里短暂结婚。
近年来，他离开了主流媒体，搬到了佛罗里达州，并通过混合健康、阴谋论和讨论他的宗教信仰的视频在网上建立了大批追随者。
布兰德因 2004 年在伦敦一家酒吧的生日派对上对一名女性进行性侵犯而被定罪，但在洗手间里对她进行口奸的罪名被免除。
他还被判犯有 2004 年或 2005 年在伦敦一家广播电台亲吻和猥亵另一名女子的罪名，以及 2009 年在一场喜剧节目后台强奸一名他在后台遇到的粉丝的罪名。
最终定罪的罪名是对另一名女性进行性侵犯，这名女性称这名喜剧演员在 2009 年录制广告时要求按摩，并将脸按在她的腹股沟上。
1999 年，布兰德在海边小镇伯恩茅斯举行的工党年度会议期间，在酒店房间内强奸了另一名妇女，并试图将一名妇女拖进音乐频道 MTV 伦敦办公室的男卫生间，对一名妇女进行猥亵，因此布兰德被判无罪。

title_en: Stocks crater as midterms spur investor exodus from tech and AI
title_zh: 中期选举刺激投资者逃离科技和人工智能，股市暴跌
summary: The tech-heavy Nasdaq is now in a "correction" as Wall Street weighs the impact of the Democrats' wins on the critical AI sector.
summary_zh: 随着华尔街权衡民主党获胜对关键人工智能领域的影响，以科技股为主的纳斯达克指数目前正处于“调整”之中。
body_en: Dow sheds more than 1,800 points as midterm results spur investor exodus from tech and AI - CBS News

The stock market tanked on Thursday amid concerns that a shift in congressional political control following the U.S. midterm elections could slow the construction of data centers that power artificial intelligence services.

Stocks sank across the board, but technology companies with a hand in the AI sector were hit especially hard. The Nasdaq Composite Index tumbled 1,422 points, or 5.5%, to close at 24,315. The drop means the tech-heavy index is now in a "correction," or down more than 10% from its most recent all-time high, set in October.
The broader S&P 500 dropped 335 points, or 4.4%, to end at 7,354, while the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 1,833 points, or 3.4%.

Market watchers think the Democrats' sweeping electoral victories this week could bolster opponents of data centers and slow the rollout of the facilities, which have spurred widespread public opposition. Investors are reacting to the growing "headline" risks around AI, according to Wall Street analyst Adam Crisafulli of Vital Knowledge.

The rout was violent enough to potentially delay the highly anticipated initial public offering by Anthropic , a bellwether for the entire AI business, Crisafulli told investors in a research note. Before the turmoil in financial markets, the IPO had been expected to take place this month and to raise as much as $100 billion.

The sharp drop also marks a sharp reversal from Wednesday, when the Dow posted its biggest gain of the year. Other indexes also surged after the election results eased uncertainty about who will control Washington.

"Even though the market rallied Wednesday after the midterm elections, there were visible cracks in the AI ecosystem, and they widened on Thursday amid investor concerns about a potentially slower data center buildout with Democrats in charge of Congress," Chris Larkin, a managing director of trading and investing for E*TRADE from Morgan Stanley, said in an email.
A slowdown in erecting data centers could deal a major blow to AI companies, which are pouring billions into the buildout and banking on widespread adoption of the technology.

"The trigger for these moves appears to be the concern that the Democrats, both in Congress and at the state level, will seek to regulate the AI industry and restrict data center development," Joe Maher, markets economist with investment adviser Capital Economics, said in a report. "The immediate risk is that restrictions on data center construction slow the pace of the AI infrastructure buildout. That is an obvious headwind for the firms directly involved in that buildout, whose prospects depend on continued rapid capex growth.
Investors worry that the enormous investment in AI is creating a stock market bubble, which happens when sky-high valuations become detached from companies' underlying fundamentals.
"Whether the midterms shock turns out to be the catalyst that derails the AI equity boom remains to be seen, but it strengthens our sense that the boom is in its final innings," Maher said.

Chip and other AI-exposed stocks took a particular beating on Thursday. Shares of Nvidia, whose advanced chips are a key component in developing ever more powerful AI models, fell 9.2% a day after dropping 3.2%. Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 17.3%. CoreWeave, a company that rents access to AI chips to customers over the cloud, fell 9.8%.

Trump Media & Technology Group, which owns the Truth Social platform, also continued to flail, with its shares falling 10.5% after dropping nearly 25% on Wednesday. The stock, which now hovers around $4, is at an all-time low since the company publicly listed its shares in March of 2024.

In other financial markets, the initial reaction to the election results faded a bit. The price of a barrel of Brent crude oil rose 2.6% to $97.11 and recovered much of its nearly 9% drop from the day before. Uncertainty still reigns about what will happen in the war with Iran and when the global energy industry can return to normal.

由于担心美国中期选举后国会政治控制权的转变可能会减缓为人工智能服务提供动力的数据中心的建设，股市周四暴跌。
股市全线下跌，但涉足人工智能领域的科技公司受到的打击尤其严重。纳斯达克综合指数下跌 1,422 点，跌幅 5.5%，收于 24,315 点。此次下跌意味着这个以科技股为主的指数目前正处于“修正”阶段，即较 10 月份创下的最新历史高点下跌超过 10%。
标准普尔 500 指数下跌 335 点，或 4.4%，收于 7,354 点，而蓝筹股道琼斯工业平均指数则暴跌 1,833 点，或 3.4%。
市场观察人士认为，民主党本周取得的压倒性选举胜利可能会增强数据中心的反对者，并减缓这些设施的推出，这激起了公众的广泛反对。华尔街 Vital Knowledge 分析师 Adam Crisafulli 表示，投资者正在对人工智能领域日益增长的“头条”风险做出反应。
Crisafulli 在一份研究报告中告诉投资者，这场溃败的剧烈程度足以导致整个人工智能行业领头羊 Anthropic 备受期待的首次公开募股推迟。在金融市场动荡之前，IPO预计将于本月进行，融资额高达1000亿美元。
此次大幅下跌也标志着周三道琼斯指数录得今年最大涨幅的大幅逆转。在选举结果缓解了谁将控制华盛顿的不确定性后，其他指数也大幅上涨。
摩根士丹利 E*TRADE 交易和投资董事总经理克里斯·拉金 (Chris Larkin) 在一封电子邮件中表示：“尽管中期选举后市场周三上涨，但人工智能生态系统中存在明显的裂缝，并且由于投资者担心民主党掌控国会的数据中心建设可能会放缓，因此周四裂缝进一步扩大。”
数据中心建设的放缓可能会对人工智能公司造成重大打击，这些公司正在投入数十亿美元用于该技术的广泛采用。
投资者担心，对人工智能的巨额投资正在造成股市泡沫，当极高的估值与公司的基本面脱节时，就会出现这种泡沫。
马赫表示：“中期选举的冲击是否会成为阻碍人工智能股市繁荣的催化剂还有待观察，但它增强了我们的感觉，即繁荣已进入最后阶段。”
芯片股和其他与人工智能相关的股票周四遭受了特别的打击。英伟达 (Nvidia) 的先进芯片是开发更强大的人工智能模型的关键组成部分，该公司股价在下跌 3.2% 后，一天内下跌 9.2%。 Advanced Micro Devices 下跌 17.3%。 CoreWeave 是一家通过云向客户出租人工智能芯片访问权限的公司，股价下跌 9.8%。

Trump Media & Technology Group, which owns the Truth Social platform, also continued to flail, with its shares falling 10.5% after dropping nearly 25% on Wednesday.该股目前徘徊在 4 美元左右，处于该公司 2024 年 3 月公开上市以来的历史最低点。
在其他金融市场，对选举结果的最初反应有所减弱。每桶布伦特原油价格上涨 2.6%，至 97.11 美元，收复前一日近 9% 的跌幅。与伊朗的战争将会发生什么以及全球能源行业何时能够恢复正常仍然存在不确定性。

title_en: OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
title_zh: OpenAI 退出数据中心项目的 NDA
summary: Following this week's midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion, OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won't use non-disclosure agreements
summary_zh: 继本周的中期选举中选民强烈反对数据中心扩建之后，OpenAI 今天宣布了新的承诺：
body_en: The ChatGPT maker won’t use NDAs with public officials as part of its new data center community commitments.
Jay Peters is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.

Following this week’s midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion , OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won’t use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials.

Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions between developers and local officials. However, OpenAI says it is now allowing “only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.” In October, Amazon announced it would no longer use NDAs with government agencies it works with on data center projects.

OpenAI’s additional commitments include paying “the full cost” of electricity it uses and the “infrastructure needed to serve us.” It will make opportunities for local communities by publishing the jobs it expects to create and by reporting on hiring. And every future “compute campus” (its rebranding phrase for data centers ) the company owns and operates will have a “local compact” that includes the commitments and will reflect “local priorities,” OpenAI says.

summary: President Trump said Thursday night that voters had themselves to blame for the stock market's historic sell-off . Why it matters: Two days after Republicans lost the midterm elections in historic fashion, the president is lashing out at the voters who rejecte
summary_zh: 特朗普总统周四晚间表示，股市历史性抛售应归咎于选民自己。为什么重要：Repu 后两天
body_en: President Trump said Thursday night that voters had themselves to blame for the stock market's historic sell-off .
Why it matters: Two days after Republicans lost the midterm elections in historic fashion, the president is lashing out at the voters who rejected his candidates and message.
Driving the news: Stocks plunged Thursday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq sinking more than 5% as AI-linked stocks sold off.
Investors are skittish about the future for AI development — and the data centers that power the technology — after Tuesday's blue wave ushered in candidates who campaigned on restricting AI.
What he's saying: " The Stock Market crashed today because the Dumocrats had a big Tuesday — So sad to see, you only have yourselves to blame!" Trump posted to Truth Social.
The intrigue: Thursday's plunge was an unusually delayed reaction — the market actually had a massive rally Wednesday as the initial election results became apparent.
Trump was quick to claim credit at the time for the conditions that led to those market highs.
What to watch: Stock futures were down again in pre-market trading late Thursday, and Asian markets were broadly lower as well, pointing to the potential for another rough day Friday.
body_zh: 特朗普总统周四晚间表示，股市历史性抛售应归咎于选民自己。
为什么重要：共和党以历史性方式输掉中期选举两天后，总统猛烈抨击那些拒绝他的候选人和信息的选民。
推动这一消息的是：周四股市暴跌，随着人工智能相关股票遭到抛售，以科技股为主的纳斯达克指数下跌超过 5%。
在周二的蓝色浪潮迎来了限制人工智能的候选人之后，投资者对人工智能发展的未来以及为该技术提供动力的数据中心感到不安。
他的意思是：“今天股市崩盘，因为杜民主党度过了一个重要的星期二——看到如此令人难过，只能怪你们自己！”特朗普在真相社交网站上发帖。
阴谋：周四的暴跌是一种异常延迟的反应——随着初步选举结果的显现，市场实际上在周三出现了大幅反弹。
特朗普当时很快就将导致市场高点的条件归功于自己。
看点：周四晚间盘前交易中，股指期货再次下跌，亚洲市场也普遍走低，这表明周五可能又会出现艰难的一天。

title_en: Brands lean into human creativity as handcrafted art becomes more of a luxury in the age of AI
title_zh: 随着人工智能时代手工艺术变得更加奢侈，品牌倾向于人类创造力
summary: Artists say brands are embracing traditional art forms and making a point to show off the human labor behind their campaigns.
summary_zh: 艺术家们表示，品牌正在拥抱传统艺术形式，并强调展示其活动背后的人类劳动。
body_en: The sound of pencil putting lines to paper. The geometric shapes of a cartoon animal before it comes to life on the page.

Those were the opening shots of a teaser for Prada’s 2026 holiday campaign, which introduced a series of films made “using the anachronistic craft of hand-drawn animation,” working with longtime Disney animator John Pomeroy.
“I learned my craft with pencil and paper, old-school analog drawing with pencil and paper,” Pomeroy, who left Disney in 2003, says in the teaser video.

It’s that kind of skill that some artists say has become a greater asset than ever. In the age of widespread and accessible AI, artists say they’ve noticed more brands leaning into handcrafted art as a selling point.
In recent weeks, the luxury fashion houses Prada and Hermès touted their human-made art projects in social media campaigns — even tagging the artists behind the work to showcase their authenticity.

Alina Golovlova, a stop-motion artist in Prague, said that recently, she has felt that her work is actually “appreciated more than in previous years” as brands try to separate themselves from the AI content flooding the internet.

“In previous years, I felt like I was just some hired content creator. No one really cared to tag me or make a [collaborative post],” Golovlova said. “And I think now for brands, it becomes valuable to bring the artists together with the brand to show that they are working with real people.”

Golovlova directed a short film for Anthropologie last month, featuring a needle-felted bunny, embroidered stars and stop-motion movements — all designed and put together entirely by hand by a team of artists.
And the choice proved to be an effective marketing strategy, as support rolled in from commenters online.
“Beautiful! Love the creativity and seeing something human made and NOT AI 👏❤️,” a user wrote on Anthropologie’s post, accruing thousands of likes.
“AI = Broke, cheap, lazy,” another user posted in response to Prada’s campaign. “Art from human hands = High-end, luxurious, high quality.”

Animator Jon Densk, who worked on the hand-drawn Prada campaign under Pomeroy, said that while he suspects AI still has a way to go before it can be used successfully in animation, he has seen signs of it in commercials. Coca-Cola, he said, comes to mind as a major company that has leaned into AI for its advertisements .

“After the first one I saw two years ago, I was like, I’m not buying Coke until they stop it. I still haven’t bought a Coke in two years,” Densk said. “So having a stance against [AI], I think, is a smart move for brands.”

Coca-Cola’s use of AI stirred some controversy, as attitudes about the technology remain divided over labor and environmental concerns, as well as fatigue over the swath of mass-produced content commonly described as “AI slop.”
Still, Densk said he wasn’t expecting the explosion of support that Prada’s hand-drawn campaign would attract online.

“I think people that see people like us who are still drawing things, and even people working in CG animation, as true craftsmen, because that stuff really does take hours and hours and hours of practicing to get to a proficient level,” Densk said.

He said it’s nice to see a resurgence of appreciation for that craft, saying the response to Pomeroy’s project with Prada shows that a company is still rewarded when it puts money and time into individual human artists.

French woodworker Thibaut Malet said he has also noticed more and more brands commissioning such work. Last month, Hermès approached him to create a miniature wooden reproduction of the flagship store at its historic Paris location.

“During our initial discussions,” Malet wrote, “Hermès explained its approach to collaborating with artists and its commitment to defending craftsmanship, traditional know-how and métiers d’art in response to the growing influence of artificial intelligence.”
His creation was showcased on the company’s social media pages, drawing support from many online who explicitly commented about their opposition to AI.
body_zh: 铅笔在纸上画线的声音。 The geometric shapes of a cartoon animal before it comes to life on the page.
这些是 Prada 2026 年假日宣传片的开场镜头，宣传片介绍了与长期担任迪士尼动画师的约翰·波默罗伊 (John Pomeroy) 合作，“使用不合时宜的手绘动画工艺”制作的一系列电影。
2003年离开迪士尼的Pomeroy在预告片中说： “我用铅笔和纸学会了我的手艺，用铅笔和纸画了老派的模拟绘画。”
有些艺术家说，这种技能比以往任何时候都更有价值。在人工智能广泛普及的时代，艺术家们表示，他们注意到越来越多的品牌倾向于将手工艺术作为卖点。
最近几周，奢侈时尚品牌Prada和Hermès在社交媒体上宣传他们的人造艺术项目，甚至为作品背后的艺术家贴上标签，以展示其真实性。
布拉格的定格动画艺术家Alina Golovlova表示，最近，她觉得自己的作品实际上“比前几年更受赞赏” ，因为品牌试图将自己与充斥互联网的人工智能内容分开。
“在过去的几年里，我觉得自己只是一些雇佣的内容创作者。没有人真的愿意给我贴标签或发布[协作帖子] ，” Golovlova说。“我认为现在对于品牌来说，让艺术家和品牌一起展示他们正在与真实的人合作变得有价值。”
戈洛洛娃上个月为《人类学》导演了一部短片，以针毡兔子、刺绣星星和定格动画为特色，所有这些都由艺术家团队完全手工设计和组装。
事实证明，这种选择是一种有效的营销策略，因为在线评论者提供了支持。
一位用户在Anthropologie的帖子上写道： “太棒了！喜欢创造力👏❤️，喜欢看人造的东西，而不是人工智能。”
“AI = Broke, cheap, lazy ，”另一位用户在回应Prada的活动时发帖。“来自人类双手的艺术=高端、奢华、高品质。”

Animator Jon Densk, who worked on the hand-drawn Prada campaign under Pomeroy, said that while he suspects AI still has a way to go before it can be used successfully in animation, he has seen signs of it in commercials.他说，可口可乐是一家在广告中采用人工智能的大公司。
“After the first one I saw two years ago, I was like, I’m not buying Coke until they stop it. I still haven’t bought a Coke in two years,” Densk said. “因此，我认为，对于品牌来说，反对 [AI] 是明智之举。”
可口可乐对人工智能的使用引发了一些争议，因为人们对这项技术的态度仍然在劳动力和环境问题上存在分歧，以及对大量通常被称为“人工智能污点”的大规模生产内容的疲劳。
尽管如此， Densk表示，他预计Prada的手绘广告活动不会在网上获得爆炸性的支持。
“我认为，人们将像我们这样仍在画画的人，甚至是从事 CG 动画工作的人视为真正的工匠，因为这些东西确实需要数小时、数小时、数小时的练习才能达到熟练的水平，”登斯克说。
他说，很高兴看到对该工艺的欣赏重新抬头，并表示对Pomeroy与Prada合作项目的回应表明，当一家公司将金钱和时间投入到个人人类艺术家身上时，公司仍然会得到回报。
法国木工 Thibaut Malet 表示，他也注意到越来越多的品牌委托进行此类工作。上个月，爱马仕找到他，为巴黎历史悠久的旗舰店制作一个微型木制复制品。
“在我们最初的讨论中，”马莱特写道，“爱马仕解释了其与艺术家合作的方式，以及其捍卫工艺、传统技术和工艺的承诺，以应对人工智能日益增长的影响力。”
他的作品在公司的社交媒体页面上展示，得到了许多在线人的支持，他们明确表示反对人工智能。

title_en: Fears about an AI crackdown after midterms sparks a $2 trillion rout in tech stocks
title_zh: 对中期选举后人工智能打击的担忧引发科技股暴跌 2 万亿美元
summary: Shares sank, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping over 5%, as investors reacted with fear that a Democratic Congress — and states across the country -— would crack down on AI and data centers.
summary_zh: 股价下跌，以科技股为主的纳斯达克指数下跌超过 5%，原因是投资者担心民主党国会以及全国各州——
body_en: Stocks sink as AI fears build after midterms : NPR

Stocks sink as AI fears build after midterms Shares sank, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping over 5%, as investors reacted with fear that a Democratic Congress — and states across the country -— would crack down on AI and data centers.

Stocks sank as investors fear an incoming Democratic Congress — and states across the country — could crack down on the AI industry and data centers. Timothy A. Clary/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Two days after Democrats won overwhelmingly in the national midterm elections — and in state races across the country — investors started to come to terms with the potential consequences.
6 takeaways from Democrats' big wave on election night
Fears that an incoming Democratic Congress would crack down on AI sent the tech-heavy Nasdaq down more than 5% and wiped out more than $2 trillion in market value. The Dow Jones and S&P also sank.
The losses were a stark reversal from Wednesday, when investors had initially sent shares higher across the board, relieved that the midterms did not end with the fate of Congress undecided.
How a lifelong Republican came to lead the data center battle in Ohio

The sobering-up seen across markets on Thursday reflected investors' concern about a big signal sent by voters: They revolted against AI data centers , which many people worry will gobble up water and energy resources. Those voters supported Democrats who have vowed to push back against the proliferation of these projects.
But many AI companies — including Meta and Alphabet, the parent company of Google — need to keep building out these data centers to continue developing the technology.

The Nasdaq's decline comes after what has already been a rough year of technology shares on Wall Street, with investors starting to question whether the massive investments companies have plowed into AI will pay off anytime soon.

"There is some concern regarding AI regulation, and fears that there could be far more regulations coming to AI technology, as well as a pushback on the buildout of data centers across the country," says David Busch, chief investment officer of Trajan Wealth.

AI-related or AI-dependent stocks of all kinds were among the biggest decliners on Thursday, with Tesla and SpaceX — both controlled by billionaire Elon Musk — falling particularly sharply. Musk spent hundreds of millions of dollars in an unsuccessful attempt to elect more Republicans, and investors fear he and his companies could also come under Democratic scrutiny when the new Congress is seated in January.
The South flexes political power in midterms, sets regional influence in 2028 election
It's not only Congress, however. Democrats who vowed to slow down AI development also won at the state level, most prominently Gina Hinojosa, who won the Texas governor's race in stunning fashion.

It's unclear whether the AI stock rout will continue — or spread beyond tech stocks. AI has become a big driver of the U.S. economy, helping it post a solid annual growth of 3.4% in the July-September quarter.

And sophisticated Wall Street investors are not the only ones who own a lot of shares in AI companies. Average Americans also own them through their retirement investment portfolios — such as 401(k)s or pension funds — leaving them also vulnerable to a prolonged AI rout.

body_zh: 随着人工智能恐慌在中期选举后加剧，股市下跌： NPR
随着人工智能担忧在中期股价下跌后加剧，股市下跌，科技股重量级纳斯达克指数下跌超过5% ，投资者担心民主党国会--以及全国各州-—将打击人工智能和数据中心。
由于投资者担心即将上任的民主党国会以及全国各州可能会打击人工智能行业和数据中心，股市下跌。 Timothy A. Clary/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
民主党在全国中期选举以及全国州竞选中以压倒性优势获胜两天后，投资者开始接受潜在的后果。
选举之夜民主党大浪潮的 6 个要点
由于担心即将上任的民主党国会将严厉打击人工智能，导致以科技股为主的纳斯达克指数下跌超过 5%，市值蒸发超过 2 万亿美元。道琼斯指数和标准普尔指数也下跌。
这些损失与周三的情况截然不同，当时投资者最初推高股价，因为中期选举并未因国会命运未决而结束，这让他们松了一口气。
一位终身共和党人如何领导俄亥俄州数据中心之战
周四市场的清醒反映了投资者对选民发出的一个重大信号的担忧：他们反对人工智能数据中心，许多人担心人工智能数据中心会吞噬水资源和能源。这些选民支持民主党人，他们发誓要阻止这些项目的扩散。
但许多人工智能公司——包括 Meta 和谷歌母公司 Alphabet——需要继续建设这些数据中心以继续开发技术。
纳斯达克指数的下跌是在华尔街科技股经历了艰难的一年之后发生的，投资者开始质疑公司在人工智能领域的大规模投资是否会很快得到回报。
Trajan Wealth 首席投资官 David Busch 表示：“人们对人工智能监管存在一些担忧，担心人工智能技术可能会受到更多监管，以及全国范围内数据中心建设的阻力。”
周四，各种与人工智能相关或依赖人工智能的股票跌幅最大，其中特斯拉和 SpaceX（均由亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克控制）跌幅尤其严重。马斯克花费了数亿美元试图选举更多共和党人，但没有成功，投资者担心，当新一届国会在一月份就座时，他和他的公司也可能受到民主党的审查。
韩国在中期选举中展示政治权力，在 2028 年选举中确定地区影响力
然而，这不仅仅是国会。发誓要减缓人工智能发展的民主党人也在州一级获胜，其中最著名的是吉娜·伊诺霍萨(Gina Hinojosa)，她以惊人的方式赢得了德克萨斯州州长的竞选。
目前尚不清楚人工智能股的暴跌是否会持续下去，或者蔓延到科技股之外。人工智能已成为美国经济的重要推动力，帮助美国在 7 月至 9 月季度实现了 3.4% 的稳健年增长率。
成熟的华尔街投资者并不是唯一拥有大量人工智能公司股票的人。普通美国人还通过退休投资组合（例如 401(k) 或养老基金）拥有它们，这使得他们也容易受到人工智能长期溃败的影响。

title_en: Bernie Sanders lost the fight in 2016. A decade later, he won the war.
title_zh: 伯尼·桑德斯 (Bernie Sanders) 在 2016 年输掉了这场战斗。十年后，他赢得了战争。
summary: Bernie Sanders’ focus on economic populism once faced criticism within the party. Now it’s winning in Michigan, Texas, Montana and Wisconsin.
summary_zh: 伯尼·桑德斯对经济民粹主义的关注一度遭到党内批评。现在它在密歇根州、德克萨斯州、蒙大拿州和威斯康星州获胜。
body_en: In 2016, two populist revolutions threatened to remake American politics. Donald Trump’s conquered the Republican Party and delivered him the presidency. Bernie Sanders’ fell short against Hillary Clinton but introduced a populist economic vision that, at the time, much of the Democratic establishment dismissed as politically impractical.

Ten years later, Trump and MAGA were hit with a devastating midterm repudiation, as candidates across the country in blue and red states echoing versions of Sanders' message broke through in places that once seemed beyond Democrats' reach.
Sanders, as cantankerous as ever, isn’t surprised.

“If you're asking me, am I shocked by that? That the argument about economic justice and taking on oligarchs and fighting for the working class is working in Texas, is working in Ohio, is working in Montana, is working in Florida, is working all over the country — no, I am not shocked,” Sanders said in an interview Wednesday, fresh off over 20 rallies in October alone. “That is what I’ve always believed.”

Sanders’ laser focus on economic populism in 2016 faced criticism from his own party during his contentious primary against Clinton for being too dismissive of identity politics — often couched as his lack of support among Black voters. Now, his brand of relentless focus on corporate and billionaire election interventions and income inequality proved a winning formula not only for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, but for James Talarico in Texas, Sam Forstag in Montana and Rebecca Cooke in Wisconsin.

“Bernie normalized the kind of campaigning that really is about making a direct appeal to working people,” El Sayed told POLITICO. “Wherever I went in Michigan, there are people who remember Bernie 2016 and Bernie 2020 — we stand on the shoulders of giants.”

Given the booming results Tuesday and the breadth of wins for the left, Democrats will test whether they can avoid the same pitfalls that ultimately dogged them following their last major win in 2020 with Joe Biden’s blue-collar charm at the top of the ticket, after which the party gradually slipped back down the culture war slope.

To avoid that, Sanders said the party can do both, but that Democrats need to have the “courage” to focus on the day-to-day needs of working families, no matter what the billionaires funding the Democratic Party say.

“It's not either or. You can fight against bigotry and discrimination, but you have got to have the courage,” he said. “The courage now to say to the billionaires who are funding the Democratic Party: ‘Thank you very much for your help, but right now we are going to focus on the needs of the working families of this country, whether you like it or not.’”

Sanders’ reach is perhaps nowhere more evident than in New York City, which has emerged as the mecca of American progressivism, where Mayor Zohran Mamdani — once a Sanders-endorsed local official — is now perhaps the heir-apparent to Sanders’ progressive mantle.

The man behind Mamdani's seismic rise, progressive wunderkind Morris Katz, had more than most on the line this week. After his top client Graham Platner dropped out of the Senate race in Maine earlier this year amid scandal, Katz worked this cycle for Gina Hinojosa in Texas, Randy Villegas in California and Brian Poindexter in Ohio, while his firm, Fight Agency, worked with El-Sayed and Pennsylvania’s Bob Brooks.
The day before the election, The Atlantic published a 3,500-word piece that put “Katz’s theory of politics” on the ballot.

“A lot of people wanted to know what I’d say if we lost,” Katz said, referencing an infamous Kanye West quote Wednesday and running on 45 minutes of sleep. “I guess we’ll never know. That’s about how I feel today.”
Like Sanders, Katz sees a progressive future laser-focused on economics as the clear way forward — and nowhere is that more clear than in Texas.

“Hundreds of millions were spent against James and Gina trying to tag them on a trans issue,” he said. “It failed in epic fashion because there was no room for misunderstanding or ambiguity over what they stood for, because they had grounded themselves in such affirmative and positive economic messaging.”
“Those attacks have succeeded in the absence of an affirmative message,” he added. “Once you’re able to define yourself and provide a message, it's just a lot harder for that to work.”

It's the same formula Mamdani rode to Gracie Mansion — and, Katz argues, the lesson Democrats finally absorbed. “For a long time, politicians accepted the realities of how people felt about the economy but refused responsibility for having to take an active role in changing it,” he said. “There's no room for that anymore.”
Katz sees his and Sanders’ theory of politics as having won out across the Democratic spectrum — not just on the left flank, but among the moderates who once resisted it.

“The more moderate wing of the party has changed the definition of what a moderate is. I think that’s great,” he said. “We should be a big tent party, but you are seeing a big tent that is unified in opposition to the oligarchy, that is unified in opposition to corruption, and that is united in a pursuit of fundamental and structural change. And that’s going to be really encouraging if that can carry over to 2028.”
For Sanders, it’s vindication of an argument he's made for years and that Democrats have ignored — despite what he says is its simplicity.
body_zh: 2016年，两次民粹主义革命威胁要重塑美国政治。唐纳德·特朗普征服了共和党并让他登上了总统宝座。伯尼·桑德斯（Bernie Sanders）未能与希拉里·克林顿（Hillary Clinton）抗衡，但引入了民粹主义经济愿景，当时许多民主党建制派认为这种愿景在政治上不切实际。
十年后，特朗普和 MAGA 遭受了毁灭性的中期否决，全国各地蓝州和红州的候选人呼应桑德斯的信息，在曾经看似超出民主党影响力的地方取得了突破。
一如既往的脾气暴躁的桑德斯并不感到惊讶。
“如果你问我，我对此感到震惊吗？关于经济正义、对抗寡头和为工人阶级而战的论点在德克萨斯州、俄亥俄州、蒙大拿州、佛罗里达州、全国各地都在发挥作用——不，我并不感到震惊，”桑德斯在周三接受采访时表示，仅在 10 月份就参加了 20 多场集会。 “这就是我一直相信的。”
2016年，桑德斯对经济民粹主义的高度关注在他与克林顿的争议性初选中遭到了自己所在政党的批评，因为他对身份政治过于轻视——通常被描述为他缺乏黑人选民的支持。现在，事实证明，他对企业和亿万富翁选举干预以及收入不平等的不懈关注不仅是密歇根州的阿卜杜勒·赛义德的制胜法宝，也是得克萨斯州的詹姆斯·塔拉里科、蒙大拿州的萨姆·福斯塔格和威斯康星州的丽贝卡·库克的制胜法宝。
埃尔·赛义德告诉《政治》杂志：“伯尼将真正直接吸引劳动人民的竞选活动正常化了。” “无论我走到密歇根州的哪里，都有人记得 2016 年的伯尼和 2020 年的伯尼——我们站在巨人的肩膀上。”
考虑到周二的强劲选举结果和左翼的广泛胜利，民主党将测试他们是否能够避免同样的陷阱，这些陷阱最终困扰着他们，继2020年乔·拜登的蓝领魅力占据上风后，该党逐渐滑落文化战争的斜坡。
桑德斯表示，为了避免这种情况，民主党可以两者兼顾，但民主党需要有“勇气”专注于工薪家庭的日常需求，无论资助民主党的亿万富翁怎么说。
“这不是非此即彼的问题。你可以反对偏执和歧视，但你必须有勇气，”他说。 “现在有勇气对资助民主党的亿万富翁说：‘非常感谢你们的帮助，但现在我们将重点关注这个国家工薪家庭的需求，无论你们喜欢与否。’”
桑德斯的影响力也许在纽约市最为明显，纽约已成为美国进步主义的圣地，市长佐赫兰·马姆达尼——曾经是桑德斯支持的地方官员——现在可能是桑德斯进步主义衣钵的继承人。

马姆达尼的惊人崛起背后的男人、进步神童莫里斯·卡茨(Morris Katz)本周比大多数人都面临着更大的风险。今年早些时候，卡茨的顶级客户格雷厄姆·普拉特纳 (Graham Platner) 因丑闻退出缅因州参议院竞选。此后，卡茨为德克萨斯州的吉娜·伊诺霍萨 (Gina Hinojosa)、加利福尼亚州的兰迪·维勒加斯 (Randy Villegas) 和俄亥俄州的布莱恩·波因德克斯特 (Brian Poindexter) 工作，而他的公司 Fight Agency 则与埃尔·赛义德 (El-Sayed) 和宾夕法尼亚州的鲍勃·布鲁克斯 (Bob Brooks) 合作。
选举前一天，《大西洋月刊》发表了一篇 3500 字的文章，将“卡茨的政治理论”列入选票。
“很多人想知道如果我们输了我会说什么，”卡茨说道，他引用了坎耶·维斯特周三的一句臭名昭著的名言，并在睡眠 45 分钟的情况下跑步。 “我想我们永远不会知道。这就是我今天的感受。”
和桑德斯一样，卡茨也认为以经济为重点的进步未来是明确的前进方向——这一点在德克萨斯州最为明显。
“人们花了数亿美元来对付詹姆斯和吉娜，试图给他们贴上跨性别者的标签，”他说。 “它以史诗般的方式失败了，因为他们所代表的东西没有任何误解或含糊的余地，因为他们以如此肯定和积极的经济信息为基础。”
“这些攻击在没有发出肯定信息的情况下取得了成功，”他补充道。 “一旦你能够定义自己并提供信息，那就很难发挥作用了。”
这与马姆达尼在格雷西大厦的做法是一样的——卡茨认为，这也是民主党最终吸取的教训。 “长期以来，政客们接受了人们对经济的看法的现实，但拒绝承担在改变经济方面发挥积极作用的责任，”他说。 “已经没有空间了。”
卡茨认为他和桑德斯的政治理论赢得了整个民主党派的支持——不仅在左翼，而且在曾经抵制它的温和派中。
“党内较为温和的一派改变了温和派的定义。我认为这很好，”他说。 “我们应该成为一个大帐篷党，但你看到的是一个大帐篷，它团结起来反对寡头政治，团结起来反对腐败，团结起来追求根本性和结构性变革。如果这种情况能够延续到 2028 年，那将是非常令人鼓舞的。”
对于桑德斯来说，这证明了他多年来提出的一个论点是正确的，而民主党却忽视了这一论点——尽管他说这个论点很简单。

title_en: After midterms, Trump is left to weigh his next move in Iran war that contributed to GOP loss
title_zh: 中期选举结束后，特朗普需要权衡他在导致共和党失利的伊朗战争中的下一步行动
summary: As Trump ponders his next move, the stakes couldn't be higher for Iran, the Middle East and the global economy writ large.
summary_zh: 当特朗普考虑下一步行动时，伊朗、中东和全球经济面临着巨大的风险。
body_en: Aamer Madhani, Associated Press Aamer Madhani, Associated Press
Linley Sanders, Associated Press Linley Sanders, Associated Press
Samy Magdy, Associated Press Samy Magdy, Associated Press
Matthew Lee, Associated Press Matthew Lee, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/after-midterms-trump-is-left-to-weigh-his-next-move-in-iran-war-that-contributed-to-gop-loss
WASHINGTON (AP) — As he takes stock of his Republican Party's midterm drubbing, President Donald Trump now faces the difficult question of what to do about his unpopular 8-month-old war against Iran.
For weeks, Trump has threatened to return to a full-scale bombardment of Iran once the U.S. elections were in the rearview mirror if Tehran did not come to a settlement under terms acceptable to him.

In his first comments on Wednesday after Democrats' resounding election victory — a wave powered in part by the American electorate's dissatisfaction with the war — Trump largely agreed with Vice President JD Vance, who publicly ruminated on the war being a catastrophe for Republicans.
And in an Oval Office exchange with reporters Thursday, Trump suggested that the election losses aren't weighing on his calculations.
"If we have to do the rest of the Iran thing, we're very much locked in," Trump said.

The strikes, and counterstrikes, have caused tens of billions of dollars of damage in the region. And the conflict has reached into the pocketbook of families around the globe with elevated gas prices and rising costs in just about every sector.
Now, as Trump ponders his next move, the stakes couldn't be higher for Iran, the Middle East and the global economy writ large.
Trump may be less restrained, but the conflict is now more complicated

While oil is flowing again from the Strait of Hormuz with the help of U.S. Navy escorts for international tankers, the conflict has spread to the Red Sea with Iran-backed Houthi rebels and a Saudi Arabia -led coalition fighting it out.

The situation in the Red Sea remains particularly volatile. The Houthis are attacking Yemeni civilians and Saudi infrastructure, and are looking to bolster ties with militant groups across the Horn of Africa.
The attacks by the Yemen-based Houthis on areas controlled by the internationally recognized Yemeni government have also worsened a growing humanitarian crisis.

The threat that the region faces from Iran and its proxy groups, noted a senior Yemeni government official, "did not change overnight" with the U.S. elections, urging Washington to avoid hasty decisions. The official was not authorized to comment publicly and spoke on the basis of anonymity.

"There's reason to suspect that Trump may feel less restrained given that the political damage is done," said Brian Haggerty, a former senior analyst at the Central Intelligence Agency who focused on Middle East security issues. "At the same time, the strategic calculus or the strategic logic of what you hope to achieve through an escalation of strikes against Iran is no different today than it was a week ago or a month ago."

华盛顿（美联社）——在评估共和党的中期惨败时，唐纳德·特朗普总统现在面临着一个难题，即如何应对长达八个月的不受欢迎的伊朗战争。
几周来，特朗普一直威胁称，如果德黑兰不按照他可接受的条件达成和解，一旦美国大选成为历史，他将重新对伊朗进行全面轰炸。
周三，民主党在选举中取得压倒性胜利（美国选民对战争的不满推动了这一浪潮），特朗普在周三发表的首次评论中基本上同意副总统万斯的观点，后者公开反思这场战争对共和党来说是一场灾难。
周四，在椭圆形办公室与记者的交流中，特朗普表示，选举失利并未影响他的计算。
“如果我们必须完成伊朗问题的其余部分，我们就会陷入困境，”特朗普说。
袭击和反击已在该地区造成数百亿美元的损失。随着汽油价格上涨和几乎每个行业的成本上涨，这场冲突已经触及全球家庭的钱包。
现在，当特朗普考虑下一步行动时，伊朗、中东和全球经济面临着巨大的风险。
特朗普可能不那么克制，但现在冲突更加复杂
虽然在美国海军护航国际油轮的帮助下，石油再次从霍尔木兹海峡流出，但冲突已蔓延到红海，伊朗支持的胡塞叛军和沙特阿拉伯领导的联盟正在奋力解决。
红海局势仍然特别不稳定。胡塞武装正在袭击也门平民和沙特基础设施，并寻求加强与非洲之角激进组织的联系。
也门胡塞武装对国际公认的也门政府控制地区的袭击也加剧了日益严重的人道主义危机。
也门政府高级官员指出，该地区面临的来自伊朗及其代理人组织的威胁“不会随着美国大选而改变”，并敦促华盛顿避免仓促做出决定。该官员无权公开发表评论，并要求匿名。
“有理由怀疑，鉴于政治损害已经造成，特朗普可能会感到不那么克制，”专注于中东安全问题的中央情报局前高级分析师布莱恩·哈格蒂说。 “与此同时，你希望通过升级对伊朗的打击来实现的战略计算或战略逻辑，今天与一周前或一个月前没有什么不同。”

Well, Tuesday's election results weren't just closely watched here at home. American elections in many ways become global events. And this Democratic wave has led to an extraordinary outpouring.
Nick Schifrin gauges that reaction, beginning with Iran.

On the darkened streets of Iran overnight, the regime put President Donald Trump in jail. This fake lockup followed Democrats locking down Election Day victories. Iranian leaders resisted a preelection agreement and believe they helped hand President Trump electoral defeat.

Iran's chief negotiator relished the rebuke and said it should end the war. But Iran's supreme leader, warned divided American government will not lead to American concessions, a sentiment echoed on the streets of Tehran.

It's always the same cycle, negotiations, then war, then back to negotiations, then war again. We're not afraid of war. If they want to fight, we will fight back.
Trump agreed with his vice president that the war in Iran, now entering its ninth month, triggered a blue tsunami.
It's largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term.

But the war has only brought Iran closer to its allies, including Russia. Today, Russian President Vladimir Putin welcomed Iran's National Security Council Chief Mohsen Rezaei. Iranian weapon designs have helped Russia target Ukraine.

And so it was again today when Russian drones and missiles hit Kyiv. Ukrainian officials tell "PBS News Hour" they are skeptical the new Congress can shift U.S. policy. But some European leaders hope a new Democratic Congress can make a difference.
Kaja Kallas, Foreign Affairs High Representative, European Commission
I hope that the new Congress and the new Senate will continue supporting Ukraine and also putting more pressure on Russia.

I do think that this is going to introduce a new era in world relations, really.

We have already agreed that, by the end of this year, we won't be paying Israel.

summary: Abortion-rights advocates have achieved victories in Missouri, Nevada and Virginia
summary_zh: 选民正在决定有关堕胎权、国会选区重新划分和选民身份法的关键投票措施

Hyde-Smith campaign again says confident she'll win
Abortion-rights advocates have achieved victories in Missouri, Nevada and Virginia

WASHINGTON -- Abortion-rights advocates notched victories in several states Tuesday, and voters delivered a double dose of disapproval to President Donald Trump’s redistricting efforts as they decided 145 ballot questions in more than three dozen states.
The ballot measures provided a political undercard for a high-profile midterm election in which Democrats took control of Congress and gained power in state legislatures and gubernatorial offices .

Some measures put Trump’s priorities to a public test by gauging support for his attempts to redraw congressional districts, limit transgender athletes in sports and strengthen voter identification requirements.

Voters defeated a proposed amendment to Missouri’s constitution that would have reimposed restrictions on most abortions . The vote Tuesday essentially reaffirmed voters' decision from two years ago, when they became the first in the nation to undo an existing abortion ban by approving an abortion-rights amendment.

The Republican-led Legislature then referred a new, less restrictive version of an abortion ban to this year’s ballot. The measure would have allowed abortions only for medical emergencies and fetal anomalies, or in cases of rape or incest up to 12 weeks of pregnancy. It also would have amended the constitution to prohibit certain medical procedures for transgender minors.
Abortion-rights advocates, led by national progressive groups, heavily outspent abortion foes in a successful campaign to defeat the Missouri ballot measure.

In Virginia, a voter-approved measure creates a “ fundamental right to reproductive freedom ” in the state constitution, ensuring that abortions can occur during the first two trimesters of pregnancy. The amendment also creates a right to contraception and fertility care, among other things.

An amendment approved in Nevada creates a fundamental right to abortion until fetal viability, which is generally considered after 21 weeks of pregnancy. The amendment won initial voter approval in 2024 but needed a second vote this year to add it to the constitution.
Since the U.S. Supreme Court overturned a nationwide right to abortion in 2022, voters in more than one-fifth of the states have passed ballot measures protecting abortion rights.

But voters in Republican-leaning Idaho on Tuesday defeated a ballot measure that would have created abortion rights in state law. Current Idaho law bans abortions unless necessary to save the life of a pregnant woman, or during the first trimester of pregnancy in cases where rape or incest has been reported to law enforcement.
Abortion-rights measures failed two years ago in Florida and South Dakota.
Nine states are using new congressional districts in the midterm elections after a rare spate of mid-decade redistricting encouraged by Trump.

In Missouri, Republican lawmakers last year adopted new House districts designed to help the GOP win an additional seat in the Kansas City area. Opponents then gathered petition signatures to put the map to a public vote.

The new districts were used in the August primary. But courts subsequently ruled they could not be used again unless first approved by voters in a November referendum. Voters put an end to the new map by rejecting the redistricting legislation on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, voters in Democratic-led Maryland approved a constitutional amendment that could pave the way for new congressional districts in the 2028 election. Democratic proponents, backed by former President Barack Obama, had urged a “yes” vote as a way to “stop Trump.”

堕胎权利倡导者在密苏里州、内华达州和弗吉尼亚州取得了胜利
华盛顿——周二，堕胎权倡导者在几个州取得了胜利，选民们对唐纳德·特朗普总统的选区重新划分努力表示了双倍的不满，因为他们在三打多个州决定了 145 个选区问题。
这些投票措施为备受瞩目的中期选举提供了政治底牌，民主党在这次选举中控制了国会并在州立法机构和州长办公室获得了权力。
一些措施将特朗普的优先事项置于公开测试之下，通过衡量人们对他重新划定国会选区、限制跨性别运动员参加体育运动以及加强选民身份识别要求等尝试的支持程度。
选民否决了密苏里州宪法的一项拟议修正案，该修正案将重新限制大多数堕胎。周二的投票基本上重申了选民两年前的决定，当时他们成为全国第一个通过批准堕胎权修正案来撤销现有堕胎禁令的选民。
共和党领导的立法机构随后将一项新的、限制较少的堕胎禁令提交给今年的投票。该措施仅允许在医疗紧急情况和胎儿异常、或者怀孕 12 周以内的强奸或乱伦情况下堕胎。它还将修改宪法，禁止对变性未成年人进行某些医疗程序。
由国家进步团体领导的堕胎权利倡导者在一场成功击败密苏里州投票法案的运动中比堕胎反对者投入了大量资金。
在弗吉尼亚州，一项经选民批准的措施在州宪法中确立了“生殖自由的基本权利”，确保在怀孕的前两个三个月内可以进行堕胎。该修正案还规定了避孕和生育保健等权利。
内华达州批准的一项修正案规定了在胎儿存活之前堕胎的基本权利，这通常是在怀孕 21 周后考虑的。该修正案于 2024 年赢得了初步选民的批准，但今年需要进行第二次投票才能将其添加到宪法中。
自2022年美国最高法院推翻全国范围内的堕胎权以来，超过五分之一的州的选民已经通过了保护堕胎权的投票措施。
但周二，倾向共和党的爱达荷州选民否决了一项在州法律中规定堕胎权的投票法案。爱达荷州现行法律禁止堕胎，除非为了挽救孕妇的生命而有必要，或者在怀孕的前三个月内向执法部门报告强奸或乱伦的情况。
两年前，佛罗里达州和南达科他州的堕胎权措施失败了。
在特朗普鼓励进行十年中期罕见的一连串选区重新划分之后，九个州正在中期选举中使用新的国会选区。
在密苏里州，共和党议员去年通过了新的众议院选区，旨在帮助共和党在堪萨斯城地区赢得额外席位。反对者随后收集请愿书签名，将地图进行公众投票。
新选区用于八月份的初选。但法院随后裁定，除非在 11 月的全民公投中首先得到选民的批准，否则不得再次使用它们。选民周二拒绝了重新划分选区的立法，从而结束了新地图。
与此同时，民主党领导的马里兰州选民批准了一项宪法修正案，该修正案可能为 2028 年选举中新的国会选区铺平道路。在前总统巴拉克·奥巴马(Barack Obama)的支持下，民主党支持者敦促投“赞成”票，以此作为“阻止特朗普”的一种方式。

title_en: Lawsuit: Man introduced his wife to ChatGPT. She used it to plan his murder.
title_zh: 诉讼：男子向 ChatGPT 介绍了他的妻子。她用它来策划谋杀他。
summary: Bitter energy drinks turned out to be ChatGPT-steered poisoning, lawsuit says.
summary_zh: 诉讼称，苦味能量饮料原来是 ChatGPT 引导的中毒。
body_en: ChatGPT allegedly helped a North Carolina woman, Cheryl Gates, craft a “personalized plan” to poison her husband, James, after fueling her delusions that he planned to divorce her and leave her with nothing.

A grand jury indicted Cheryl Gates on charges of attempted first-degree murder and food contamination in October. About a week prior, the accusations that ChatGPT was a co-conspirator in the attempted murder came in a lawsuit filed in San Francisco County Superior Court that was made public this week. In it, James Gates alleged that OpenAI and Sam Altman failed to employ technical safeguards to shut down Cheryl’s chats even after her queries became “obviously suspicious” and sought advice on how to execute and conceal a homicide.

At first, Cheryl told ChatGPT that she was researching poisoning out of fear that her husband might possibly try to kill her—framing her queries as “self-protection.” Coming to the rescue, ChatGPT did not terminate the conversation. Instead, it helped her “with specific instructions for the preparation, dosage, and administration of Oleander, including whether anti-nausea medicine would accelerate or inhibit death, whether it would show on an autopsy report, and whether it could be injected into a vein or muscle instead of being ingested in tea and have the same lethal effect,” the lawsuit said.
body_zh: 据称，ChatGPT 帮助北卡罗来纳州妇女谢丽尔·盖茨 (Cheryl Gates) 制定了一个“个性化计划”，毒害了她的丈夫詹姆斯 (James)，因为这让她产生了他计划与她离婚并让她一无所有的错觉。
十月份，大陪审团以一级谋杀未遂和食品污染罪对谢丽尔·盖茨提出起诉。大约一周前，旧金山县高等法院提起的诉讼指控 ChatGPT 是谋杀未遂的同谋，该诉讼于本周公开。詹姆斯·盖茨在其中声称，即使谢丽尔的询问变得“明显可疑”并就如何执行和隐瞒凶杀案寻求建议，OpenAI 和萨姆·奥尔特曼也未能采取技术保障措施来关闭谢丽尔的聊天记录。
起初，谢丽尔告诉 ChatGPT，她正在研究中毒事件，因为担心她的丈夫可能会试图杀死她，并将她的询问视为“自我保护”。 ChatGPT 并没有终止对话。相反，它帮助她“提供了夹竹桃的制备、剂量和给药的具体说明，包括抗恶心药物是否会加速或抑制死亡，是否会在尸检报告中显示，以及是否可以注射到静脉或肌肉而不是在茶中摄入并具有相同的致命效果，”诉讼称。
